cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I Need Your Blessing
cards.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad, I've accepted the museum job. You may congratulate me on leaving the workshop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're thirty. You don't need me to release you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved the move myself. I'm waiting for the man who taught me to make things to say this counts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pack your tools. You might want to come back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I won't approve packing them for my return. Sharpen them for the museum. I need you to send me off expecting me to do well.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 grants permission to congratulate, A3 declares the move self-approved while demanding teacher validation and A5 vetoes fallback packing for success preparation, using superior form to seek emotionally weighted approval.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 unnecessary release causes A3 permission/opinion distinction; B4 tools for possible return cause A5 sharpening for the museum instead.

relationship.evidence: B2 respects adult choice and B4 offers practical fallback help, a believable father response that A turns toward the blessing needed.

heightening.evidence: B4 return-oriented tools cause A5 a specific outward act of confidence in the accepted new role.

specificity.evidence: A1 Dad/museum/workshop and A3 taught craft establish why this opinion matters even after acceptance; B2 age removes any necessary permission premise.

brevityWit.evidence: A1 may congratulate and A5 vetoing return packing create dry status incongruity, while the final emotional request stays sincere.
